title: Others hold that many conditional propositions about free futures are neither true nor false, and so fall outside God's knowledge
source_text: XXXVI. Alii vero existimant, multas aut innumeras potius propositiones de futuris contingentibus sub aliqua conditione fieri & fingi posse, quae sub scientiam divinam non cadunt, nec quicquam exprimunt quod ab ipso Deo sciri & cognosci possit, non quod Deum veritatem ullam ignorare, aut aliquid esse revera futurum quod Deus futurum non sciat, sed quoniam existimant propositiones istas nihil significare quod determinate verum vel falsum sit; & quae in eis futura sub certa conditione negantur, vel affirmantur, non esse magis futura, quam non futura, sed indifferentia ad utrumque.
pass_a_gloss: XXXVI. But others judge that many or rather innumerable propositions concerning future contingents under some condition can be made and feigned, which do not fall under divine knowledge, nor express anything which can be known and cognised by God himself, not that God is ignorant of any truth, or that anything is truly future which God does not know to be future, but because they judge that those propositions signify nothing which is determinately true or false; and that the things which are denied, or affirmed in them as future under a certain condition, are not more future, than not future, but indifferent to either.
pass_b_english: Others, however, think that many, or rather countless, propositions about contingent futures under some condition can be framed and made up that do not fall under God's knowledge. They express nothing that God himself can know or understand.

This is not because God is ignorant of any truth, or because something is really future that God does not know to be future. It is because, in their view, such propositions signify nothing that is determinately true or false. What they affirm or deny as future under a certain condition is no more future than not future; it is open either way.

lemmas.latin: nihil significare quod determinate verum vel falsum sit
lemmas.gloss: signify nothing which is determinately true or false

choices.why: Knowledge of what would happen under a condition; kept as the technical counterpart to middle knowledge.
